The business trades across two separate Amazon storefronts — a main store and a specialty store — each with its own order flow and its own pricing behaviour. items.text: A Handover That Stalled, and FBM Orders That Never Showed Up

Wonderfold came to Folio3 mid-flight. The company was moving away from a previous integration partner, and the transition itself had become the problem — the handover introduced complications into an integration that still had to keep running. A second issue was biting at the same time, in production, where it hurt most.
The transition to a new integration partner led to complications in the integration process, leaving the work part-finished and the path forward unclear.
Fulfilled by Merchant (FBM) orders were delayed in the live environment. The orders were not appearing as expected, which caused further delays in order fulfilment downstream.
The client's environment was locked down enough that another solution provider had not been able to complete the work inside it.

What Wonderfold needed was not a fresh start. It was a partner who could pick up a part-built integration in a restricted environment, finish the transition cleanly, and make Amazon orders — all of them — appear in Business Central reliably.

items.text: One Connector, Two Amazon Stores, One ERP

Folio3 customized its Burq connector to integrate the client’s complex JSON files with both Amazon and Business Central. The connector reads the JSON files, passes the data into Business Central, and fetches information from Amazon to sync it back. The company change was resolved and the transition completed. The FBM job was corrected and processed on live client orders, after which FBM orders synchronized and processed successfully in the live environment. What Folio3 delivered:
Burq connector customized to the client's JSON structure
Amazon to Business Central order and data sync
A second integration for the Amazon specialty store
Specialty store orders priced from the Business Central item price
FBM job corrected and validated on live client orders
Transition from the previous integration partner completed
Delivered inside the client's restricted environment
A platform ready for additional ERP and ecommerce connections

items.text: The client brought two candidate approaches to the table. Folio3 provided 100% of the input to identify the most suitable implementation, and proposed the Amazon to Business Central integration as the optimal solution — delivered in two parts, each handling a different storefront and a different pricing rule.
The core integration, syncing order and item data between the main Amazon store and Business Central, with the Burq connector reading the JSON files and passing the data into BC.
Amazon to Business Central — Specialty Store

For the specialty store, the price shown against an order is not the order price but the item price set in Business Central for that order — so what the storefront displays stays aligned with what Business Central holds.
The connector was customized to read the client's complex JSON files, pass the data into Business Central, and fetch information from Amazon to sync it with BC.
Burq is a one-stop solution for the full range of integration needs: multiple connections can be established, and any Microsoft ERP can be integrated with any ecommerce platform.
